clues: This small town sits on a deep, narrow bay on the south coast of Alaska. A long road leads north from here to Anchorage.
A huge sheet of ice near this town is slowly pulling back. Its shrinking edge is called a clear sign of climate change.
This town takes its name from the man who led the deal to buy Alaska. He bought the land from Russia in the year 1867.
Trains from the far north end their long run here at the sea. This is the last stop on the whole rail line.
On the shore at the south end of town stands Mile 0. It marks the start of the famed old trail north.
